transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-18
Start time (UTC): 14:00
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ellen (QuantCare MLOps), Samir (QuantCare CTO), Leah (QuantCare Security), Tom (QuantCare Infra)

Summary: QuantCare is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production inference of clinical triage models. Primary drivers: isolation (PHI), predictable latency for 99th pct under bursty traffic, and meeting healthcare compliance (SOC2/ISO). They want hybrid reserve: reserved GPUs for steady workload + burst guardrails.

Topics discussed: reserved capacity sizing, tenant isolation and pre-warm strategies, VPC/private deployment vs on-prem, KMS/encryption and audit logs, pricing model for reserved + burst, SLOs and fallback to hosted during maintenance, pilot/POC criteria.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. mirroring the invite — I'm Maya, account exec. We also have Diego and Priya from solutions and infra. How about quick intros on the QuantCare side?
[00:12] Ellen: Hi, Ellen Park, I run MLOps at QuantCare. We own infra for models in prod.
[00:17] Samir: Samir Gupta, CTO. I focus on compliance and budget approvals.
[00:21] Leah: Leah Owens, SecOps, I'll be vetting logs, key mgmt, and data residency.
[00:27] Tom: Tom Reyes, infra, I'll own network and private connectivity.
[00:31] Diego: Great, thanks. Outline for today: sizing, isolation, compliance questions, and next steps for a pilot.

[02:05] Ellen: Quick context — we run several clinical triage models, mostly long contexts ~2k tokens for patient notes, average request rate is around 600 qps daytime spikes to 3k qps briefly after batch jobs, so burstiness is a real concern. We need 99th percentile latency under 450 ms for user-facing flows.
[02:37] Maya: Got it. Are these models latency-sensitive at the token level or overall response time?
[02:44] Ellen: Overall response. Some responses hit 1.5k tokens so per-token optimizations help but end-to-end matters.

[04:10] Diego: On Redwood Dedicated we typically layer reserved pools for steady throughput and enable a hotpool/prewarm for bursts. For 600 steady qps we'd recommend reserving N GPUs and then set a burst budget that can spin up additional capacity or fallback to compatible model variants. Question — is PHI staying in your VPC/on-prem or are you ok with encrypted-at-rest in hosted?
[04:45] Leah: PHI cannot leave our control per our contract with hospitals; we prefer private deployment in our VPC or an on-prem install. Key management must integrate with our HSM/KMS.
[05:02] Priya: Good to know. We support VPC Private deployment and an on-prem package. KMS integrations with common HSMs can be arranged; audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM. There are some small differences in autoscaling latency for on-prem.

[06:20] Samir: Pricing question up-front — how does reserved billing vs burst billing work? We want predictable monthly commit for reserved but still need the option for on-demand burst.
[06:34] Maya: Reserved is a committed monthly capacity price; bursts are either prepaid burst credits or usage overage at a higher per-hour rate. We can model a hybrid where you hold, say, 70% steady reserve and leave 30% for burst that is billed if used. Diego will give a concrete estimate.

[07:55] Tom: Network — our infra is air-gapped for some environments. Can Redwood deploy fully on-prem with no egress to Redwood control plane? That's a hard requirement for a subset of tenants.
[08:12] Diego: Yes, we have an on-prem private deployment that can operate in air-gapped mode. The tradeoff is you manage updates and certain telemetry. We can provide a private control plane option that talks over customer VPN for management but the model execution can be fully contained.

[09:48] Leah: Audit logs: we need immutable logs for every inference request for at least two years, and fine-grained RBAC. Do you store request payloads in any retention by default?
[10:05] Priya: By default Redwood logs minimal metadata for observability; request payloads are optional and configurable. For private/on-prem we can configure logs to ship to your SIEM and set retention policies. We support RBAC and SSO integrations (SAML/Okta).

[11:30] Ellen: Operational question — if the reserved pool is saturated during a spike, what's the fallback? We can't afford to drop requests silently.
[11:42] Diego: Typical patterns: 1) automatic warm pool prewarmed nodes to absorb burst, 2) graceful degradation by routing to a smaller/quantized model variant with lower latency, or 3) spillover to Redwood hosted endpoints if allowed. For your PHI constraints, spillover to hosted is probably not allowed, so warm-pool + model variant is primary. We can also queue with prioritized lanes.

[13:05] Samir: For canary rollouts and model versioning, do we get environment pinning so that canaries aren't touching production data?
[13:15] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports environment pinning and traffic splitting; you can run a canary in an isolated VLAN or separate tenant node. We also support shadow traffic for evaluation without impacting production.

[14:40] Ellen: Latency — you mentioned prewarming. How long does a prewarm take and what's the cost of keeping a warm pool?
[14:55] Diego: Prewarm times vary by hardware and model size; typically 30–90s for a big model if cold, but hotpool nodes kept alive can accept requests under tens of ms. Cost is essentially the reserved GPU/node-hour cost; you can keep a small number of hotpool nodes active 24/7 or use an autoscaler with a min hotpool count.

[16:10] Tom: Our infra team is concerned about noisy neighbors if we run multiple tenants per GPU. We prefer physical isolation for certain models that handle PHI. Can Redwood guarantee dedicated tenancy?
[16:25] Maya: Yes, Dedicated offers physical isolation options — fully single-tenant nodes for an additional premium. There's also tenant fencing and GPU partitioning options if you want to multiplex with software guarantees.

[17:40] Leah: KMS — can we bring our own keys and rotate them on schedule? Also MFA for key access?
[17:51] Priya: BYOK is supported; rotations can be orchestrated via your KMS/HSM. MFA for key management access is handled through your identity provider and RBAC controls.

[19:05] Ellen: For the pilot, we'd like to scope a representative workload: 600 steady qps, simulated daytime bursts to 3k qps for 5–10 min, model size 13B quantized, target p95 < 350ms, 99th < 450ms. We want both VPC Private and an on-prem feasibility path tested.
[19:30] Diego: That's a clear POC. For 13B quantized models the compute profile is moderately high — we'll propose X reserved nodes and a warm pool to cover bursts. I'll calculate based on your QPS and token lengths.

[20:55] Samir: Compliance — you mentioned SOC2, do you have ISO27001? Our infosec prefers both.
[21:04] Maya: Redwood maintains SOC 2; ISO is in progress on some product lines. We'll attach current attestations. For private/on-prem, many of the compliance controls fall under your remit; we provide tools and docs to support audits.

[22:30] Leah: Data residency — some patient data must remain in EU. We have US and EU clusters; if we run in our VPC in EU that's fine. Is region pinning supported?
[22:42] Priya: Yes, you can pin to regions and we also support routing policies so traffic from EU tenants is served in EU-only capacity.

[23:55] Ellen: How do you handle software updates for on-prem mode? We need maintenance windows and rollback plans.
[24:05] Diego: For on-prem we ship a packaged upgrade; customers can schedule upgrades. There's a canary upgrade flow and rollback. For Private (VPC) deployments we coordinate rolling upgrades across your reservation windows.

[25:48] Tom: Network topology — we need support for private endpoints and no egress to internet for inference traffic. Do you support customer-managed NAT or VPC endpoints?
[26:00] Priya: Yes, we support private endpoints, VPC peering, and customer-managed NAT. For fully air-gapped installs, we provide an installation profile that does not require outbound egress.

[27:20] Ellen: Observability — we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards. Is that in the console for private deployments?
[27:31] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console features can be configured to send telemetry to your Grafana/Prometheus or we host it in the private plane depending on deployment.

[28:55] Samir: One risk — what if our node goes down mid-shift? RTO expectations?
[29:05] Diego: For Dedicated with redundancy we design across failure domains. Recovery depends on topology; single-tenant nodes have longer warm-up if new nodes need to be created. We recommend a small redundant pool in another AZ or region for critical workloads.

[30:40] Ellen: We also need to ensure tokenization and PII scrubbing before logs leave the inference runtime. Is that configurable?
[30:51] Priya: Yes, you can configure preprocessors to scrub or hash PII before logging. For private/on-prem you can disable payload logging entirely.

[32:12] Maya: To align on the pilot scope: Diego and I will size reserved + warm pool, provide cost scenarios, and Maya will send compliance docs. QuantCare to provide traffic histograms and SLOs. Any other items?
[32:28] Leah: Please include detailed KMS/HSM integration notes — we use a Thales Luna HSM.
[32:35] Tom: And include network playbook for air-gapped install.

[33:10] Diego: Noted. Also, competitor note — if you evaluate Databricks or others, the main differentiator here is the production-first failover patterns and hybrid private control plane.
[33:30] Samir: Good. Budget — if we commit on a 12-month reserved contract, what's typical discount band?
[33:40] Maya: Discounts scale with committed spend — we'll include an illustrative pricing matrix in the follow-up.

[34:55] Ellen: Timeline — we'd like to run a 4-week pilot in January. Is that feasible?
[35:04] Diego: Yes, January pilot is feasible. We'll need your traffic and model artifacts by Dec 28 to prepare. On-prem install might add lead time depending on procurement of hardware.

[36:30] Leah: Security review — need to run a short questionnaire and maybe an architecture call with your security engineer.
[36:38] Maya: We'll attach the security questionnaire and set that meeting with our security lead.

[37:50] Tom: Are there any limits on model sizes or custom kernels in private? We have some optimized kernels we want to bring.
[37:59] Priya: You can bring custom kernels but we test compatibility. On-prem gives you more control, but we'd advise a small qualification window.

[39:05] Ellen: Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[39:10] Diego: Watch out for underestimating warm pool needs; cold starts for large models are expensive in latency. Also, on-prem telemetry and patching processes require more operational effort.

[40:20] Maya: Recap of next steps: Maya send SOC2/ISO + security pack, Diego send cost/throughput estimate, QuantCare send traffic histograms and model artifacts. Schedule technical deep-dive late December/early January.
[40:42] Ellen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[40:47] Samir: Thanks.
[40:49] Leah: Thanks.
[40:51] End of call.

Notes: Slight transcription errors present in speaker labels, some words auto-corrected. References to Redwood product APIs sometimes abbreviated (hotpool/hot pool, KMS spelled K M S). Links shared during call: (1) SOC2 PDF link placeholder: https://redwood.example/soc2.pdf (2) Private deployment guide: https://redwood.example/private-deploy-guide.pdf
